question: Which gland releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone to trigger the female reproductive cycle?
explanation: The hypothalamus initiates the hormonal cascade by secreting gonadotropin-releasing hormone, which stimulates the pituitary gland. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h1)

question: What happens when the hormonal feedback loop between the brain and ovaries stops working properly?

options.A: Blood pressure drops to dangerous levels
options.D: Endocrine and structural health problems can develop

explanation: Any imbalance in the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis leads to menstrual irregularities and other reproductive disorders. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h1)

question: What term describes the absence of menstruation for three months or more in a woman with previously normal cycles?
explanation: Secondary amenorrhea is defined by the cessation of established menses for a prolonged period, typically three months or more. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why does dysmenorrhea cause painful cramping in the lower abdomen during menstruation?

options.A: High levels of uterine prostaglandins trigger strong muscle contractions
options.B: Ovarian cysts rupture spontaneously at the start of every cycle
options.C: Bacterial infections multiply rapidly in the acidic vaginal environment
options.D: Increased estrogen levels cause sudden fluid retention in the pelvic cavity

explanation: Prostaglandins trigger intense uterine muscle contractions and blood vessel narrowing, resulting in the characteristic pelvic pain of dysmenorrhea. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h2)

question: What are uterine fibroids mainly made of?
explanation: Leiomyomas or fibroids are benign tumors originating from the smooth muscle layer of the uterus, known as the myometrium. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h3)

question: What is the main cause of pelvic organ prolapse in women?

options.A: Rapid overgrowth of the inner uterine lining
options.B: Weakening of pelvic floor muscles and supporting ligaments
options.C: Bacterial infection of the upper fallopian tubes
options.D: Excessive production of luteinizing hormone by the pituitary

explanation: Pelvic organ prolapse happens when supportive structures like muscles and ligaments stretch or weaken, failing to hold pelvic organs in place. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h3)

question: Which physical examination finding is most typical of pelvic inflammatory disease?

options.B: Pain when the cervix is moved during examination
options.D: Hard abdominal mass felt during palpation

explanation: Cervical motion tenderness, or pain when the cervix is moved during a bimanual exam, is a classic sign of pelvic inflammatory disease. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h4)

question: Why is early treatment of pelvic inflammatory disease so important for women of childbearing age?

options.A: To eliminate benign smooth muscle tumors completely
options.B: To reverse the abnormal hardening of the uterine wall
options.C: To stop sudden weight gain caused by hormonal imbalance
options.D: To prevent permanent tube scarring and future infertility

explanation: Untreated infections cause inflammation that leads to scar tissue formation in the fallopian tubes, increasing risks for infertility and ectopic pregnancy. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h4)

question: Which viral infection is strongly linked to the development of cervical cancer?
explanation: Persistent infection with high-risk strains of human papillomavirus is the primary causative factor in the development of cervical dysplasia and cancer. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h5)

question: Why is ovarian cancer frequently diagnosed at a late, advanced stage?

options.A: Routine blood tests can easily detect malignant cells early
options.B: Early symptoms are mild and deep pelvic organs are hard to feel during exams
options.C: Tumors develop rapidly only after menopause occurs
options.D: Patients always experience severe pain in the first few weeks

explanation: Ovarian cancer produces subtle, non-specific symptoms like bloating, making early clinical detection very difficult during routine exams. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h5)

question: What is the main reason for performing an endometrial biopsy in a patient with abnormal bleeding?

options.B: To treat an acute pelvic infection

explanation: Histological examination of endometrial tissue obtained via biopsy helps identify or rule out hyperplasia and cancerous changes. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h6)

question: Which nursing action is most important before a patient undergoes a routine pelvic examination?

options.A: Insisting that family members remain in the room at all times
options.B: Placing the patient face down on the examination table
options.C: Explaining the procedure clearly to reduce anxiety and build trust
options.D: Giving strong pain medication to prevent all discomfort

explanation: Clear explanation and privacy foster patient comfort and cooperation during sensitive physical examinations. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is the term for the surgical removal of uterine fibroids while preserving the uterus itself?
explanation: A myomectomy specifically targets and removes fibroids while keeping the uterus intact for women who wish to retain fertility. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h7)

question: How do hormonal medications help manage conditions like endometriosis or heavy menstrual bleeding?

options.A: By regulating the cycle and slowing down abnormal tissue growth
options.B: By dissolving large ovarian cysts within hours
options.C: By destroying bacteria located in the upper reproductive tract
options.D: By strengthening the pelvic floor muscles directly

explanation: Hormones modulate the endometrium and suppress ovulation, reducing excessive bleeding and the growth of hormone-sensitive lesions. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h7)

question: What type of exercise should a nurse teach a patient to help strengthen supportive pelvic floor muscles?
explanation: Kegel exercises involve contracting and relaxing the pelvic floor muscles to improve tone and support pelvic organs. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h8)

question: Why is patient education about regular Pap smears essential in community health nursing?

options.A: To prevent the spread of bacterial infections like chlamydia
options.B: To eliminate hormone changes that cause severe cramps
options.C: To measure exact hormone levels in the blood
options.D: To catch early cell changes before cancer develops

explanation: Routine screening identifies cervical dysplasia early, allowing for timely intervention before invasive cancer can take hold. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T10#GNS311_U1_T10_h8)
